Tree search

Lesson 42's agent needed thousands of games to fill a value table. Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) needs no training at all. Before each move it plays out many imagined games from the current board, grows a tree of the positions it visits, and steers new simulations towards moves that have done well. Planning, done at decision time.

You are O. MCTS is X. On X's turn, run simulations and watch the numbers on the board: visits $N$ for each move (large) and X's average result through that move, $Q$, with a win scoring 100% and a draw 50% (small). Then let X play its most visited move.

The puzzle: O threatens the right column. Only one move avoids losing. With 10 simulations MCTS finds it about half the time. By 50 it almost always does. Try $c = 0$ too: with no exploration term, a move that loses its first rollout may never be tried again.

The maths

Each node of the tree is a board $s$ with a visit count $N(s)$. Each edge, a move $a$ from $s$, stores $N(s, a)$ and $W(s, a)$, the total result of simulations through it (1 for a win, $\tfrac12$ for a draw, 0 for a loss, for the player making the move). Its average is $Q(s, a) = W(s, a)/N(s, a)$. One simulation has four phases:

  1. Select. From the root, repeatedly take the move $\arg\max_a \big[ Q(s, a) + c \sqrt{\ln N(s) / N(s, a)} \big]$.
  2. Expand. At the first move not yet in the tree, add one new node.
  3. Simulate. Play random moves to the end of the game.
  4. Back up. Add 1 to $N$ and the result to $W$ on every edge of the path.

Step 1 is UCB from Lesson 9 applied at every node (the UCT rule, Kocsis & Szepesvári, 2006): $Q$ exploits, the square-root term explores moves tried rarely. Each player picks the move best for itself, so the tree approximates minimax search. As the number of simulations grows, UCT's choice at the root converges to the minimax move.

After the simulations, MCTS plays the move with the most visits. Visits are a steadier signal than $Q$, which can be high for a move tried only a few times.

MCTS is a rollout algorithm with memory (S&B §8.10–8.11). Values exist only for the current search: the tree is thrown away after the move (or its relevant subtree kept). Nothing is learned between games. Lesson 96 adds learning.
